hook: We spent 3 weeks rebuilding our multi-agent memory pipeline. Here's why simple vector search failed us:
content:
We spent 3 weeks rebuilding our multi-agent memory pipeline. Here's why simple vector search failed us:

When we launched our first agent, semantic search worked fine for 50 documents. But as soon as users started asking about temporal context ('what did we decide last Tuesday?'), standard RAG collapsed.

Here are 3 architectural shifts we made:
1. Episodic vs. Semantic splitting
2. Reflection loops on task completion
3. Structured state cache alongside agent memory

If you're building agents today, don't treat vector DBs as human memory. They are fundamentally different.

hook: I almost shut down our startup 6 months ago. The metric that saved us wasn't MRR.
content:
I almost shut down our startup 6 months ago. The metric that saved us wasn't MRR.

It was weekly retention of power users. We were obsessing over top-of-funnel signups, but ignoring the fact that our best 10 users were using the product 4 hours a day.

When we pivoted our roadmap solely to delight those 10 people, word of mouth kicked in.

Lesson: Find your obsessive 1%, and build exclusively for them first.

hook: Our MongoDB cluster hit 99% CPU during launch week. One missing compound index cost us $4,200.
content:
Our MongoDB cluster hit 99% CPU during launch week. One missing compound index cost us $4,200.

We were querying posts by brandId and sorting by createdAt descending. Without `{ brandId: 1, createdAt: -1 }`, Mongo was doing full collection in-memory sorts for every user dashboard render.

Once added, query latency dropped from 1,200ms to 4ms, and cluster CPU stabilized at 12%.

Never deploy query pipelines without inspecting `.explain('executionStats')` first.

hook: How we decreased our LLM token costs by 64% without losing response quality:
content:
How we decreased our LLM token costs by 64% without losing response quality:

1. Dynamic prompt pruning: We stripped conversational history older than 3 turns into a single summary vector.
2. Model routing: Simple classification tasks run on Flash (cheap & fast); only synthesis and strategy run on Pro models.
3. Semantic caching for repeated intent patterns.

Result: Lower latency, lower bills, happier users.

hook: How a single uncaught Promise rejection caused 28 minutes of API downtime yesterday:
content:
How a single uncaught Promise rejection caused 28 minutes of API downtime yesterday:

At 14:15 UTC, our worker process crashed repeatedly because a background webhook fired without a try/catch block. In Node 20+, unhandled rejections terminate the process by default.

What went wrong:
1. Health check was green because the main web server was up
2. PM2 restart limit was exceeded on the worker

Fix applied: Added process-level safety boundaries and isolated queue workers into separate Docker containers.

Post-mortem shared openly because reliability is built in daylight.

hook: The 'Chain-of-Density' prompt pattern that doubled our automated summary accuracy:
content:
The 'Chain-of-Density' prompt pattern that doubled our automated summary accuracy:

Instead of asking the LLM to summarize once, you prompt it over 5 progressive iterations:
• Step 1: Write an initial draft containing 1-3 key entities.
• Steps 2-5: Compress the length while adding 1-3 missing salient entities without increasing word count.

The resulting summaries are dense, highly informative, and contain zero fluff.

Full prompt template in the snippet below. Try it on your next document analysis pipeline.

hook: We ran 500 autonomous agent tasks across 3 LLM models. Here are the failure rates:
content:
We ran 500 autonomous agent tasks across 3 LLM models. Here are the failure rates:

• Tool hallucination: 18% in baseline models vs. 3% when using strict schema validation.
• Infinite retry loops: 24% when agents are not given an explicit step quota.
• State drift: 31% after 10+ conversation turns without memory consolidation.

Takeaway: Agent autonomy is 20% prompt engineering and 80% deterministic guardrails.

hook: Why we deleted 12,000 lines of microservices code and went back to a modular monolith:
content:
Why we deleted 12,000 lines of microservices code and went back to a modular monolith:

With 4 engineers, managing 8 repositories, Docker compose files, Kubernetes manifests, and gRPC contracts was taking 40% of our week.

We consolidated into a single clean Node/TypeScript monorepo with domain boundaries.

Results:
• CI/CD build time dropped from 14 mins to 90 seconds
• Zero distributed transaction bugs
• Faster onboarding for every new hire

Don't adopt Google-scale architectural complexity before you have Google-scale engineering headcount.
